messages:
Anna_Sales: Hey — spinning up a POC with Orbital Health. 6-week POC timeline, customer asks for a mixed GPU pool: 4x H100 + 8x A100-equivalent. They want autoscale to 3x baseline for normal traffic and occasional demo bursts up to 6x. Asking for a short-term commit + preferential burst rates during the POC. Also pushed a security questionnaire (SOC2 + KMS questions). Can we sketch pricing and what needs deal-desk approval?
Mike_Solutions: quick Qs — what's the workload profile? avg seq len, percent long-context, and expected concurrency? that drives whether H100 benefits kick in vs A100.
Anna_Sales: workload: mainly text generation + occasional reranking. avg seq ~1k tokens, peaks around 2k for batches. Estimated steady concurrency ~80-120 rps during demos (spiky), ~10-20 for day-to-day. Model is an open 13B tuned model.
Mike_Solutions: ok. Suggestion: propose a tiered commit: baseline reserved pool that maps to 8 A100-equivalent slots (covering steady state) + explicit autoscale headroom (autoscale to 3x baseline) with an agreed burst cap and a separate burst rate. Example calc snippet to present to customer:
```
Baseline: 8 x A100-equivalent slots (reserved)
Autoscale target: up to 24 concurrent slots (3x)
Burst cap: up to 48 slots for demos (6x)
Pricing sketch: baseline rate = $12/hr/slot, autoscale multiplier = 1.15, burst multiplier = 1.6
Monthly baseline hours ~ 8 slots * 24 * 30 = 5760 slot-hours
Baseline monthly = 5760 * $12 = $69,120
Estimated autoscale incremental = billed at baseline*1.15 only when used
Burst billed at baseline*1.6 when used
```
These numbers are placeholders — need DealDesk to sanity-check thresholds and final multipliers.
Sarah_DealDesk: heads-up on discounting — for committed spend this size (baseline ~ $70k/mo) we typically evaluate a committed discount band. Standard bands: 10% for pilot-scale monthly commits, 15–25% for larger 12+ month commits. POC promos: we can offer a one-time POC credit (5–10%) + a conditional 6-month conversion discount if they convert to a 12-month reserved commit. I need final ARR estimate to apply tier. Please flag any non-standard burst concessions (e.g., waived burst surcharge) — those require approvals.
Leo_Ops: operational notes: autoscale and burst are fine but we need to lock in two things before giving softer burst prices: 1) a hard network egress guard and 2) an agreed burst budget cap to prevent runaway costs. Also billing behavior: burst usage is metered in 15-min increments and billed at the burst multiplier. We can offer a limited ‘demo grace’ (e.g., first 4 demo hours per month at autoscale multiplier instead of full burst), but that’s a special ops concession and should be listed in the deal.
Priya_Legal: for the security questionnaire: we can send SOC2 report and KMS/HSM attestation. Customer also requested proofs around VPC peering and SSO/SCIM provisioning. We need Orbital to sign the standard DPA + a short appendix covering the POC data handling (retention, deletion). If they want an SLA for POC demos, legal needs the commit/term length and the specific SLO numbers to be explicit.
Anna_Sales: got it. For the customer pitch doc I’ll include Mike's rate sketch and call out the demo grace and conditional conversion discount. Sarah — can you confirm what discount band we can pre-approve for the AE to verbally offer?
Sarah_DealDesk: I can pre-approve up to 12% off baseline for POC + a one-time $10k pilot credit without exec sign-off. Anything beyond that (deeper discount, waived burst surcharge, or extended grace) needs deals-manager + finance sign-off. I'll start an internal approval thread and tag finance.
Mike_Solutions: small technical follow-ups for the POC spec: please capture expected token throughput/day and a representative prompt set (we use that to decide quantization/kv-cache config). Also note if they plan heavy reranking or embeddings — that changes slot math.
Anna_Sales: token throughput ~50k tokens/day; reranking happens in ~5% of requests. I'll attach sample prompts and the security questionnaire PDF to the deal thread.
dealbot: [system] created internal ticket DD-8231 for deal-desk approval + ops runbook request. Link: https://internal.redwood/company/deals/DD-8231 :white_check_mark:
Leo_Ops: Recommend adding a concrete burst cap number to customer proposal (e.g., burst cap = 48 slots / 1000 demo-minutes per month) — that avoids surprises. Also we'll need a short runbook (who to page if autoscale fails).
Priya_Legal: also add data residency checkbox — they require EU-only data for POC. Need to confirm region mapping and whether we can pin to eu-west-1. Ops, can we guarantee that for the POC?
Leo_Ops: yes we can pin pool to eu-west-1 for the POC, but note that mixed GPU inventory might mean H100 instances come from a different AZ. We'll document the topology in the runbook.
Anna_Sales: perfect. I'll draft a customer-facing proposal with baseline numbers + the conditional conversion incentive and the explicit demo burst cap. Sarah — once you have the deal-desk note, please tag me and I'll present to the customer tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Sarah_DealDesk: will do. Escalating now — tagging @finance and @deals-manager. :eyes:
Anna_Sales: thanks all — will push the draft in #deals-orbital and attach the questionnaire.
__metadata_note: This thread is intentionally concise and focused on pricing + deal-desk routing for a dedicated commit with autoscale/burst concessions. Messages are chronological and mimic Slack style.
